\chapter{Hablábamos --- The Imperfect Gets Its Plural}
\label{ch:hablabamos}
\hlchaptermodality{243}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use every person of the -aba imperfect.}

I can use every person of the -aba imperfect.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[hablábamos]{hablábamos — the imperfect gets its plural}

\label{lesson:ES-C63-hablabamos}



\begin{quote}
\emph{Hablaba} — I used to speak, or I was speaking. The tense for what was going on.

Until now you have had only its singular.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the three that were missing}]
Say them: \emph{nosotros} \emph{\textbf{hablábamos}}. \emph{Vosotros} \emph{\textbf{hablabais}}. \emph{Ellos} \emph{\textbf{hablaban}}.

The \emph{-aba-} runs all the way through. The endings on top of it are the ordinary plural ones you have used since the present tense: \emph{-mos}, \emph{-is}, \emph{-n}.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
Now look at the accent on \emph{\textbf{hablábamos}}, because it is the only one in the set and it is doing real work.

The word ends in \emph{-s}, so Spanish's default would put the stress on the \textbf{next-to-last} syllable: \emph{habla-BA-mos}. But the stress actually falls a syllable earlier, on the \emph{-BA-}... which is not where the default lands, so the accent has to say so.

Without it you would read \emph{hablabamos} with the wrong beat. The mark is not decoration; it is the difference between the word being a past tense and being nothing at all.

None of the other five needs one, because in each of those the default already lands where the stress is.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{hablábamos}, \emph{hablabais}, \emph{hablaban}
  \item all six, straight through
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which of the six carries a written accent? (Only \emph{\textbf{hablábamos}}.)

And what would go wrong without it? (The \textbf{stress} would land in the wrong place.)
\end{tcolorbox}
